name: PT Red Planet Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Red Planet Indonesia — asset-heavy budget hotels, priced for a story it has not delivered
frontmatter.summary: PSKT owns a small portfolio of budget and midscale hotels whose revenue is flat, whose costs still swallow the gross margin, and whose only anchor is a property book worth a fraction of the market price. After restating depreciation to the audited total, EBITDA is better than the pack showed but the equity is still worth far less than the shares: SELL.
thesis: Nine-month revenue is flat year on year while direct costs fell double digits — the refit programme is working on cost, not on demand.
Restating depreciation to the full audited charge lifts FY2025 EBITDA to a low-twenties margin, but net profit stays negative through the forecast.
The company has no bank debt and cash on the balance sheet, but also a large accumulated deficit and no dividend history.
Book value per share is the only defensible asset anchor, and the market pays several times it for a loss-making operator.
The November share-price move came with no disclosed fundamental catalyst and coincided with other group names; we do not underwrite it.

catalysts.event: Completion of the Pekanbaru and Surabaya refits and the Pusako interior work
FY2026 audited results: first full year without the Pusako hotel in the base
Any disclosed corporate action — asset sale, rights issue or group injection — that would change the equity base

blocks.text: **SELL. Target Rp15 against a price of Rp228, a return of -93.3%.**

PSKT is a small Indonesian hotel owner-operator. It runs budget and midscale hotels under the Monoloog brand and one four-star property, the Pusako in Bukittinggi [S2]. After the Red Planet Holdings exit the company sits inside the Happy Hapsoro group, and the current board is running an asset-rejuvenation programme it describes as value-driven [S2].

The variant view is simple. The market is paying for a transformation narrative; the accounts show a business whose revenue has stopped growing, whose cost base is still far too heavy for its asset size, and whose profit and loss line has been negative for years. The one thing of value is the property portfolio, carried at 338.6 of property, plant and equipment, against total equity of 322.0 at the last year end [S5] and 319 IDR bn at 30 September 2026 [S4].

What moves the value: occupancy and average room rate at the renovated hotels, and the pace at which general and administrative costs fall from the current level. Neither has yet shown up in revenue. Direct costs did fall sharply in the first nine months of 2026, which is why the operating loss narrowed [S4]; that is the single genuine positive in the file.

The stock is not cheap on any measure that survives contact with the accounts. On our central case the discounted cash flows are worth Rp14 per share, an earnings multiple on restated EBITDA gives Rp10, and a sales multiple gives Rp17. The weighted target is Rp15. Book value is 31.1 per share and is discussed as a cross-check, not as the answer: a buyer of the buildings would pay for them only net of the operating losses that come with them.

PSKT builds, owns and operates hotels in Indonesia. Its portfolio was rebranded from Red Planet to Monoloog Hotel with effect from May 2023 [S5]. The group also owns the Pusako Hotel in Bukittinggi, a four-star property with a heritage building, which the company has been renovating and which stopped operating in the fourth quarter of 2025 [S5][S2].

The directly held hotel entities in the consolidated accounts cover Surabaya, Pekanbaru, Palembang, Makassar, Bekasi, Solo, Tangerang, Depok and the Jakarta head office, plus the Pusako vehicle [S5]. That is a national footprint across Java, Sumatra and Sulawesi, concentrated in secondary cities where budget and midscale demand comes from domestic business travel rather than international tourism.

Revenue is almost entirely rooms. The revenue note splits room, food and beverage, management service, space rental and other sales [S5]. A small management-service line is earned from PT Cityloog Utama Internasional, a related party, under a cooperation agreement signed in 2024 under which PSKT provides resources to manage the Cityloog hotel and receives a basic fee of a percentage of gross operating revenue plus a share of the incentive fee [S5]. That line is related-party revenue and should be read as such.

The strategy is asset rejuvenation, not expansion. Palembang was refreshed in 2023 and Solo in 2024, Makassar in 2025, with Pekanbaru and Surabaya plus the Pusako interior scheduled for 2026, including digitalisation of IT services and utility efficiency [S2]. The company has said the programme needs substantial capital expenditure but is value-driven and should compress operating costs [S2]. Nine-month 2026 direct costs of 16.8 IDR bn against 52.3 of full-year 2025 revenue show that the cost side of that promise is being delivered; the revenue side is not.

Scale is small. Revenue was 52.3 in FY2025, down from 55.1 in FY2024 [S5]. Employment is small but not as small as the data pack says: the FY2025 filing reports 137 persons permanent employees plus ten contract staff at the end of 2025 [S5], against the 90.0 the pack carries. The difference matters only because it shows how thin the central overhead is relative to the property base — this is an owned-asset business, not a people business.

The controlling shareholder group is the Happy Hapsoro business group [S2]. Insider holdings are 80.1% of shares and the free float is 19.5% [S0]. The group affiliation matters for governance and for the way the shares trade, and we treat it in the governance section [S0].

Indonesian budget and midscale hotels are a volume business. Demand is driven by domestic travel, which is large and grows with the middle class, and by corporate travel into secondary cities. Supply is fragmented: national chains, regional operators and independent owners all compete on price and location, and online travel agencies control a growing share of the booking funnel [S2].

The competitive position of PSKT is weak but not hopeless. The Monoloog format is a clean, cheap, standardised room in a secondary city — a genuine product in a market where consistency is scarce. But the company has no distribution advantage, no loyalty programme of scale and no pricing power. Its own disclosures describe optimising OTA partnerships and influencer marketing as the route to higher revenue [S5], which is the language of a price-taker.

Five forces, briefly [S2]. Rivalry is high and rising as new budget supply opens in the same secondary cities. Buyer power is high because guests switch on price and OTA ranking. Supplier power is moderate: property is owned or leased long-term, but labour and utilities are local and rising. Substitutes are strong — budget travellers substitute into homestays and apartments. New entrants are easy at the low end, which caps returns on any renovated asset.

Market size and growth are hard to pin down from company disclosure, which publishes neither occupancy nor revenue per available room [S5]. What the filings do show is a fragmented secondary-city market in which the company's own route to growth is marketing rather than new rooms: the refit budget goes into digitalisation, utility efficiency and online travel agency partnerships rather than into new keys [S2][S5]. That is a share-shift strategy in a market that grows with domestic travel, and it is why we treat revenue growth here as an execution variable rather than a market tailwind.

The moat question is therefore about property, not brand [S5]. What PSKT owns is a set of buildings on long leases or freehold land in city-centre locations. That is a real asset and it is what the balance sheet carries at 338.6. It is not a compounding franchise: returns on the assets are below the cost of capital, which is why the equity has been eaten away by losses.

Macro context matters less here than for most consumer names [S0], because the customer is domestic, but the rupiah and the rate cycle still affect the cost of capital and the valuation multiple. The house macro desk has Indonesian rate-sensitive consumer discretionary names on avoid, which is consistent with our view of the demand backdrop for a discretionary stay.

Budget hotel economics are usually described through revenue per available room, occupancy and the ratio of fixed to variable cost. A hotel with high fixed costs benefits strongly from incremental occupancy once it passes its break-even point, and a renovation that lifts both rate and occupancy can move a property from loss to profit quickly. The reverse is also true: a property that loses its demand base carries its depreciation whether or not the rooms are sold.

Revenue fell from 55.1 in FY2024 to 52.3 in FY2025 [S5], and the nine months to September 2026 came in at 37.5 IDR bn against a marginally higher prior-year comparative [S4]. Growth has stopped. The exit of the Pusako hotel from operations explains part of the decline and will not repeat in the FY2027 base [S5].

Gross margin was 52.5% in FY2025 and above half in the first nine months of 2026, as direct costs fell to 16.8 IDR bn for nine months after a double-digit year-on-year decline [S4]. The improvement comes from cost control, not from pricing.

The cost problem is general and administrative expense: 36.2 in FY2025 against revenue of 52.3, an operating loss of -8.6. G&A was 25.0 IDR bn in the first nine months of 2026, still more than two-thirds of revenue [S4]. For a hotel operator of this size, that is the whole story: the properties generate a reasonable gross margin and the centre consumes it.

The critical data correction in this file is depreciation. The data pack shows a charge of a fraction of the audited number because Indonesian filings use the direct cash-flow method. The audited fixed-asset note allocates the FY2025 charge in two parts, 9.1 IDR bn to direct costs and 10.8 IDR bn to general and administrative expense, and the FY2024 parts are 9.3 IDR bn and 10.1 IDR bn [S5]; the sums are 19.9 IDR bn and 19.4 IDR bn, which are the figures we restate into the model's depreciation line. The nine-month 2026 split is 7.2 IDR bn plus 7.5 IDR bn, giving 14.7 IDR bn [S4]. We restate G&A to the note total as well, so the model's EBITDA is revenue less direct costs less G&A plus the full charge: 11.2 for FY2025, a margin of 21.5%. Each of the six components carries its own verbatim quote; the LK prints no single total row, because the allocation table's numbers do not extract with its labels, so the facts file stores the components and their exact sum rather than a total the source does not print. Any analysis that uses the pack's EBITDA without this correction is wrong by roughly the size of the entire depreciation charge; an earlier draft of this report made exactly that error and this version corrects it.

Cash flow is weak even on the corrected EBITDA. Operating cash flow was an outflow of 1.7 IDR bn in FY2025 [S5], against 11.2 of EBITDA — a cash-conversion gap of roughly the size of the EBITDA itself. The bridge is largely working capital and the other receivable: at the end of 2024 the company carried a 34.3 IDR bn other receivable from PT Soros Samudera Sejahtera, arising from the 2020 sale of its Karya Bangun Hotelindo shares, and it collected 27.7 IDR bn of that receivable during 2025 [S5]. That collection is a one-off recovery of old sale proceeds, not a hotel disposal and not recurring cash. The remaining balance was small by the end of 2025, so the receivable overhang is largely resolved; the cash-conversion gap it created in the reported year is not permanent, but neither is it repeatable income.

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the company. Cash at end-2025 was 23.3 [S5], and the bank loan was fully repaid during the year, leaving debt of 4.0 at the balance-sheet date and no bank debt at the September 2026 date [S5][S4]. Net debt is negative at -19.3. Against that, equity is 322.0 and the accumulated deficit disclosed in the going-concern note is large [S5]. The company has liquidity but no earning power. A further 140 IDR bn of property and equipment is fully depreciated but still in use at September 2026 [S4], which is why book depreciation overstates the cash reinvestment the portfolio needs.

Forecast assumptions, all sourced in the assumption file [S4][S5][S2]: revenue flat in FY2026 at the nine-month run-rate, then a recovery as renovated assets return; gross margin held at the 2026 level and improved by a point; G&A fading from 66.3% of revenue toward 61.5%; depreciation starting at 37.5% of revenue and declining as the absolute charge is held broadly flat against growing revenue; capex starting at 8.0% and settling at 10.0% for a rolling refurbishment cycle; no tax because of the deficit; no dividend.

On those assumptions the company stays loss-making at the net line through the forecast period [S0]. EBITDA is positive and grows, but depreciation of a third of revenue keeps operating profit negative or barely positive. This is not a cautious assumption set: it gives management credit for the full cost programme, holds gross margin at the improved level and assumes revenue growth resumes at a rate above the last two years.

Earnings quality. **Accruals ratio, (net profit less operating cash flow) over average total assets, FY2023 to FY2025** [S8][S5][S0]: the numerator is negative in all three years. FY2023 net profit was -10.7 against 2.0 IDR bn of operating cash flow; FY2024 was -7.0 against 4.7 IDR bn; FY2025 was -12.6 against an outflow of 1.7 IDR bn. On an asset base of 372 IDR bn the ratio therefore sits at a low single-digit percentage and is negative — the opposite of the profit-outruns-cash pattern the screen is built to catch. The negative sign is mostly the depreciation charge rather than conservatism: EBITDA was 11.2 while operating cash flow was an outflow, and the gap is the working-capital and receivable swing described above, not revenue recognition. The FY2024 operating cash flow is the 4.7 IDR bn reported in the FY2024 statements; the FY2025 LK carries the comparative slightly lower after a reclassification [S8][S5].

**Divergence flags**: receivables did not outgrow revenue — the opposite happened, because the 34.3 IDR bn other receivable from PT Soros Samudera Sejahtera was collected down by 27.7 IDR bn during 2025 [S5]; inventory is immaterial for a hotel operator; there are no capitalised development costs. Cash conversion rather than accrual inflation is the issue, and it is disclosed.

**IDX regime flags**: no special notation or monitoring-board reference appears in the filings, the pack or the press we archived, but the pack carries no board-status field and IDX's own site refuses automated access, so we record this as unverified rather than cleared [S0][S5].

**Related-party gravity**: revenue from PT Cityloog Utama Internasional under the management agreement was 0.3 IDR bn, about half a per cent of revenue, with a small related receivable [S5]. The material related flow was the Soros receivable above, which peaked at about two-thirds of a year's revenue; it is now largely collected, which reduces but does not erase the governance question about how group assets move in and out of this company.

**Structure flags**: no pledge over the controlling stake is disclosed in any note we searched; the only pledge in the filing is land and buildings pledged by a subsidiary as collateral for a bank loan that has since been repaid [S5]. No rights issue, private placement or buyback is disclosed [S5][S3]. The auditor is KAP Kanaka Puradiredja Suhartono, a Nexia network affiliate, reappointed at the annual general meeting for a fee of 0.6 IDR bn with no non-audit services [S3]; that is a second-tier firm, and the opinion page itself did not extract from either archived document, which we treat as an information gap rather than a finding [S3][S5].

**Classification**: the going-concern note is a disclosed, optics-class flag — management states the losses and the accumulated deficit and sets out a marketing and cost plan [S5]. We found no manipulation-class flag: no fabricated cash, no fictitious revenue, no restatement of prior accounts. The single missing input is the exchange's own board status, which we flag openly rather than assert.
On those checks the earnings-quality screen does not kill the name [S5]; the valuation does.

The method set fits a loss-making but asset-heavy hotel operator. A discounted cash flow is the primary method because the value of the company is the cash the hotels can produce after maintenance capex. EV/EBITDA is a cross-check now that the denominator is sound: on the corrected total depreciation, FY2025 EBITDA is 11.2, not the fraction the pack showed. EV/Sales is the third cross-check because a negative net profit and a small EBITDA make earnings multiples fragile, while revenue is stable and disclosed. We do not use P/E — earnings are negative — and we do not apply a peer P/B multiple: the engine's peer median was above two times book, and paying a premium for a book that earns a negative return is exactly the error this revision corrects. Book value is shown below at a haircut, as an asset cross-check.

Cost of capital. The build is a risk-free rate of 7.4%, less the sovereign default spread of 1.6% that the house macro deck nets out of the local risk-free rate, plus an equity risk premium for a mature market of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, multiplied by an unlevered beta of 0.90. With no debt in the capital structure, the cost of equity is 11.9% and the WACC is 11.9%. The arithmetic is 7.4% minus 1.6% plus 0.90 times the sum of the two premia; the default-spread netting is the line the previous draft omitted.

Primary method. The DCF values the operating cash flows over the explicit horizon and a terminal value at 3.5% growth, giving Rp14 per share and an enterprise value of IDR 111.4 bn. The terminal value is 45.1% of the total, which is high because the explicit years carry heavy refurbishment capex and the terminal year normalises it. We tested the DCF with terminal capex equal to depreciation: that removes most of the terminal free cash flow and cuts the value sharply, which is why the capex-to-depreciation gap is the largest judgement in this file. Our position is that book depreciation of a third of revenue overstates cash reinvestment, because 140 IDR bn of the asset base is already fully depreciated and the refit cycle runs near 10.0% of revenue [S4][S5]. A reader who capitalises the full book charge gets a lower value; the direction of the call does not change.

Growth, returns and the multiple-survival test. This is not a compounding franchise and we do not value it as one. **Reinvestment** — capex less depreciation plus the change in working capital, over NOPAT — is negative in every forecast year: capex settles at 10.0% of revenue against a depreciation charge of 31.1%, or IDR 6.5 bn against IDR 20.4 bn, with working capital held at -30.0% of revenue [S4][S5]. **ROIIC** is therefore not a positive number we can defend: incremental revenue earns an EBIT margin of -5.9% at the end of the horizon, so additional sales still destroy value at the margin. **Fade**: with no excess return there is no fade date to set — the explicit horizon is itself the fade, and the value rests on the terminal year, where growth is 3.5% against a WACC of 11.9%. **Multiple survival**: the terminal value is 45.1% of enterprise value, and with terminal-year EBITDA of IDR 18.3 bn the implied exit EV/EBITDA sits above the 6.5 entry multiple, so part of the DCF is multiple expansion rather than cash. We accept that because the terminal year normalises capex against a real property base; a reader who does not accept it should treat the cross-check range, not the DCF, as the answer, and the call only gets worse for the stock.

Cross-checks. The EV/EBITDA method gives Rp10 at 6.5 times restated FY2025 EBITDA, -26.6% below the DCF; the multiple is a peer median applied to a still-depressed year, so it is a floor rather than a central estimate. The EV/Sales method gives Rp17 at 2.7 times sales, 22.0% above the DCF, and it is the cross-check closest to the market's own framing of the story. Neither reaches the share price.

The blend gives Rp15 before the final check and Rp15 as the target, against a price of Rp228. The gap between methods is itself the finding: the range from Rp10 to Rp17 spans the operating value of the business, and the market price sits far above the top of it.

The asset cross-check. Reported equity at 30 September 2026 is 319 IDR bn [S4] — not 322.0, which is the 31 December 2025 figure [S5]. On the 10,351.2 million shares in issue that is a book value per share far below the Rp228 price, and the shares trade at 7.3x the FY2025 book of 31.1 [S0]. A ten per cent haircut for the closed Pusako hotel and the aged Pekanbaru and Surabaya plant leaves nine-tenths of book, and twenty per cent leaves four-fifths; both are below the market price but above our target, deliberately: book is what the assets cost less depreciation, not what a buyer pays for a business that loses money operating them. We do not weight book into the target — the corporate template has no adjusted-book method, and paying a premium to a book that earns a negative return on equity is the error this revision corrects. A sale or redevelopment at or near book would be worth more than our bull case; no buyer, price or timetable is disclosed, so we carry it as a signpost rather than a scenario. Weights are the industry default of six-tenths DCF, a quarter EV/EBITDA and the balance EV/Sales, with EV/Sales substituted for P/E because earnings are negative.

What today's price implies. At Rp228 the market capitalisation is 2,360,080,813,008.0 [S0]. Our DCF gives an enterprise value of IDR 111.4 bn; add the net cash on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet and that becomes an equity value of Rp14 per share [S4]. The two denominators must be kept apart: the price is a large multiple of the enterprise value of the whole business, and a smaller but still extreme multiple of the equity value, because our enterprise value sits below our equity value once net cash is added. Reverse-engineering the DCF, the price requires FY2027E revenue growth of 44.7% against the 7.0% in our base case — a step-change no filing discloses — or a terminal value that assumes the property base is redeveloped at a multiple of its carrying value. Either way the market is paying many times the operating value our cash-flow work supports.

The two inputs that carry most of the value are the G&A ratio and the revenue growth rate after the refits [S4]. A one-point change in the G&A ratio moves the DCF value by more than a point of revenue growth, because the cost base is so large relative to revenue. That is the honest summary of this business: it is a cost story, not a growth story [S4].
Downside risks, with likelihood and impact.

Regulatory and listing risk, medium likelihood and high impact: the company's going-concern disclosure, its small free float and the concentration of ownership leave it exposed to special monitoring or notation if conditions deteriorate [S5][S0].
Macro and FX, medium and medium: the customer is domestic, so a rupiah shock hits costs and the discount rate more than demand.
Operational, high and high: the refit programme is the whole plan, and any slippage in Pekanbaru, Surabaya or the Pusako delays the only route to profitability [S2].
Commodity, low: no direct commodity exposure beyond utilities.

Governance, medium and high: the group affiliation, the related-party management agreement and the absence of a fundamental catalyst behind a sharp share-price move are all governance-relevant [S5][S7].

Liquidity and financing, medium and high: the free float is 19.5% and the register is concentrated [S0]; with negative operating cash flow and a going-concern note, a rights issue or a related-party loan is a real bear-case path, and either would dilute or subordinate minorities.

Balance-sheet risk, medium and high: the Pusako hotel has been closed since the fourth quarter of 2025 and its property has not been written down; an impairment of a fifth of that asset would cut book value by about a tenth, and the Soros receivable was once large enough to matter even though most of it has now been collected [S5].

Scenarios. The bear and bull cases shock the same three drivers by mirrored amounts: revenue growth by three points, gross margin by one and a half points and the G&A ratio by two points, in opposite directions [S4][S5]. The base case carries half the probability and the tails are symmetric. Both cases are earnings-only. An earlier draft also shocked a book-value haircut in both directions; we have dropped it because no weighted method uses book value, so the shock moved nothing — the outputs are unchanged — and a dead shock is worse than no shock. For the same reason the bull does not claim a portfolio sale or a group injection at book: that route would be worth more than our bull case, but no buyer, price, timetable or transaction is disclosed, so it stays a signpost and an asset cross-check. On the earnings shocks the bear is worth Rp12 and the bull Rp19 against a base of Rp15. The bear is a genuine downside test, not a rounding of the base, and the bull tests the cost programme working without any asset-sale rescue.

Signposts that would change the view: a sustained rise in revenue per available room at the renovated hotels; G&A falling below the level we forecast; a property sale or redevelopment at or above book; a capital raise or asset injection that changes the equity base; and any regulatory or listing action. We would revisit the rating if the price fell toward the asset cross-check while the operating loss narrowed.

Ownership is concentrated. Insiders hold 80.1% and the free float is 19.5% [S0]. The company is affiliated with the Happy Hapsoro group [S2], a structure that in Indonesia typically means related-party transactions and asset-injection optionality, both of which cut against minority holders unless priced.

Related parties, quantified. Management-service revenue from PT Cityloog Utama Internasional was 0.3 IDR bn in FY2025, about half a per cent of revenue, and the related trade receivable was small [S5]. The larger related-party item historically was the 34.3 IDR bn other receivable from PT Soros Samudera Sejahtera at the end of 2024, equal to about two-thirds of that year's revenue, of which 27.7 IDR bn was collected in 2025 [S5]. A receivable of that size from a related sale of shares deserves scrutiny; the collection reduces the concern but does not eliminate it.

Audit. The FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Kanaka Puradiredja Suhartono, a Nexia KPS network firm, with Syamsudin as signing partner, for a fee of 0.6 IDR bn and no non-audit services [S3]; the firm was reappointed at the annual general meeting to audit FY2025 [S3]. The auditor's report wording itself is not in our archive: the opinion page did not extract from either the annual report or the FY2025 financial statements, so we cannot tell an unqualified-with-emphasis opinion from a qualified one. We flag that as an information risk to a SELL thesis that relies on the going-concern disclosure and would close it before any position is taken.

Dividends: none in the price history and none declared; the company carries a deficit [S0][S5]. Buybacks: we found no buyback announcement in our sources and have removed the catalyst an earlier draft cited; the small rupiah item in the filings that was mistaken for one is a time deposit.

Board and management: the FY2025 annual report, signed in April 2026, lists Suwito as President Director and Astini Bernawati Oudang as Director, with Dinno Indiano as President Commissioner and Adang Ruchiatna Puradiredja as Independent Commissioner [S3]. We make no claim of a board change in 2026 because we could not source one.

Pledges, notation and rights issues: we found no pledge disclosure in the notes we searched, no pending rights issue and no special notation in the pack [S5][S3]. The pack carries no board-status field and the exchange site refuses automated access, so this is unverified rather than cleared.

ESG: the company's own disclosure frames the refit around utility efficiency and green operations [S2], which is the main environmental lever for a hotel owner. Social exposure is employment in secondary cities. Governance is the dominant ESG issue here, not environmental performance.

Dated catalysts: completion of the Pekanbaru and Surabaya refits and the Pusako interior work through 2026 [S2]; the FY2026 audited results in the first quarter of 2027 [S4]; and any disclosed corporate action — an asset sale, rights issue or group injection — which is the only plausible route to a price near book [S7]. We do not include a buyback because we could not source one.

KPIs we watch [S4]: quarterly revenue and the direct-cost trend from the LK; the G&A ratio including its depreciation allocation; occupancy and average rate if disclosed; the cash balance and any new borrowing; related-party revenue and receivables; and any change in the share register or listing status. We also watch monthly price and volume against the free float, because a thin register can move the shares far from value without operating news.

The share price rose sharply in November 2026 alongside other companies in the same group, with market reporting noting the absence of a clear fundamental catalyst for the move [S7]. We do not underwrite price momentum. Our view changes when the operating numbers change, and on the current evidence they have not.

bear.narrative: Domestic travel stays soft, the Pekanbaru and Surabaya refits slip a year and the refit costs land in operating expenses, so growth is three points lower, gross margin one and a half points lower and the G&A ratio two points higher than in the base case. The bull case mirrors these shocks. Earnings-only. The asset route (portfolio sale at book) is a cross-check, not a scenario and not shocked here.

bull.narrative: The refit cycle lifts occupancy and average room rate, the nine-month 2026 cost base holds after the direct-cost and G&A reduction, and the renovated Pekanbaru, Surabaya and Pusako assets ramp a year faster, so growth is three points higher, gross margin one and a half points higher and the G&A ratio two points lower than in the base case. The bear case mirrors these shocks. The asset route (portfolio sale at book) is a cross-check, not a scenario.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 is flat on the nine-month run-rate (9M 2026 revenue 37.54 IDR bn vs 37.69 a year earlier, -0.4%) with the Pusako hotel out of service for the whole fourth quarter against a Q4 2025 that carried two months of it; FY2027+ reflects the renovated Pekanbaru, Surabaya and Pusako assets returning and the domestic-demand plan, then fades to terminal growth.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 gross margin is 55.2% after direct costs fell 11.8% year on year; we hold that and add a point as the renovated rooms ramp, never above the 9M 2026 print.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: G&A was 66.5% of revenue in 9M 2026 and 70.2% in 9M 2025; the renovation and digitalisation programme is the only credible route to the low-60s, so we fade it there rather than to a hotel-sector norm.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Total depreciation from note 11 is 19.86 IDR bn in FY2025 (9.09 direct + 10.78 G&A) or 37.9% of revenue, and 14.67 IDR bn in 9M 2026 (39.1%); holding the absolute charge near 19.6-20.3 IDR bn against rising revenue gives the declining ratio path below, ending at 28% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 7.2% of revenue and LTM capex 12.2% during the Makassar/Pekanbaru/Surabaya refits; we keep 8% in FY2026 and settle at 10% for a nine-hotel refurbishment cycle. Book D&A (38% of revenue) overstates cash reinvestment because 139.8 IDR bn of assets are already fully depreciated, so capex never equals D&A.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Hotels run negative operating working capital (guest prepayments and OTA settlement); the pack shows -0.30x revenue and we hold it flat.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The group is loss-making with an accumulated deficit of 339.6 IDR bn at end-2025, so no cash tax is payable on the forecast horizon; the pack tax line is a deferred-tax artefact.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has ever been paid and the company carries a 339.6 IDR bn deficit; all cash is retained for the refit programme and the announced buyback.

assumptions.label: Haircut to reported book value (asset cross-check only)
assumptions.basis: Book equity is the value floor only if the assets are worth carrying value; we apply a 10% haircut for the closed Pusako hotel, whose 338.6 IDR bn of PP&E was not written down, and for the aged Pekanbaru and Surabaya plant, leaving 90% of the 30 September 2026 book of 318.6 IDR bn. The corporate template has no weighted adjusted-book method, so this haircut feeds the asset cross-check only and is not shocked in the scenarios, because no weighted method moves with it.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Indonesian long-run nominal GDP growth is well above this, but a budget-hotel operator with a fixed property base and no pricing power should not carry a GDP terminal rate; 3.5% is below the house IDR terminal growth default of 4%.

challenges.challenge: F4/F5/F10 restate D&A from the direct-cost allocation only. Note 11 (S5 p54-55) allocates FY2025 depreciation into direct cost 9.0876bn (note 23) and G&A 10.7760bn (note 24), total 19.8636bn; 9M2026 note 10 allocates 7.1699bn direct and 7.4983bn G&A, total 14.6682bn (S4 p47). FY2025 EBITDA is therefore about 11.2bn (21.3% margin), not 0.47 (0.9%), and 9M2026 EBITDA about 10.4bn (27.8%), not 7.8%. The model da_pct 18.5% should be about 38-39%, so the central EBITDA barely positive thesis, the calibration gate, the Rp2 EV/EBITDA value and the DCF are all understated by ~10.7bn a year.
challenges.answer: Restated total D&A to 19.86 FY2025 and 14.67 9M2026 from both allocations, set da_pct 37.5% fading to 28%, reran; FY2025 EBITDA 11.15 and the target is rebuilt [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF is misread. The report says the market capitalises the company at roughly 0.4 times the value our cash-flow work supports, but model reverse_dcf.implied_value is 0.4356, the implied FY2027E revenue growth (43.6%) needed to justify Rp159, and market cap 1,645.8bn is 20.6 times the DCF equity value of 79.76bn (Rp159 vs Rp7.7/share). A 0.4x multiple would mean the stock is undervalued; the true statement is the opposite.
challenges.answer: Replaced the unit error: reverse DCF now shows implied FY2027E growth of 44.7% against 7% and market cap against DCF enterprise value [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report says the DCF terminal value is at 0.0 growth. Model valuation.g is 0.035 and assumptions terminal_growth is 3.5%; the placeholder formats 0.035 as 0.0. With terminal value at 54.9% of EV, this misstates the primary method's key input and a reader cannot reproduce Rp8.
challenges.answer: Terminal growth is now formatted as a percentage so section 4 reads 3.5% and reconciles to assumptions terminal_growth [S0].

challenges.challenge: P/B is 35% of the blend and supplies Rp66 of the Rp30 target, yet the same paragraph argues a rational buyer of a loss-making hotel group would not pay a premium to book. Applying 2.15x to a negative-ROE, going-concern name is unjustified; at 1.0x book the P/B value is ~Rp31 and the target falls to ~Rp16. The target Rp30.3 is also below the Rp31.1 book value the report calls the floor, and the P/B metric uses 30 June 2026 book (Rp30.68/share), not the Rp31.1 cited.
challenges.answer: Removed P/B from the blend rather than pay 2.15x for a negative-ROE book; book is a haircut cross-check at nine-tenths and four-fifths of equity [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA applies 6.54x to FY2025A EBITDA of 0.467, a trough that is itself understated by the D&A error; on corrected EBITDA (~11.2) the method gives ~Rp9, not Rp2. The report calls EBITDA a poor denominator yet gives the method 20% weight.
challenges.answer: EV/EBITDA now runs on restated FY2025 EBITDA of 11.24 at 6.5x giving Rp10, carrying its default 25% weight as a cross-check [S5].

challenges.challenge: Scenarios shock only revenue growth and gross margin. Section 4 says the two inputs that carry most value are the G&A ratio and revenue growth; G&A is not shocked, and the 35%-weight P/B/book value is not shocked either. Bear Rp28.7 vs base Rp30.2 is a 4.8% cut for a narrative (refits slip a year, G&A near 70%) that should be far more severe; doubling bear probability still gives ~Rp29.9.
challenges.answer: Scenarios now shock the G&A ratio and book haircut alongside revenue and margin, mirrored bear and bull; the bear cuts the target to Rp12 from Rp15 [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: The COE build does not reproduce 11.9%. 7.45% + 0.90 x (4.23% + 2.46%) = 13.47%; the engine's 11.85% nets out a 1.62% default spread that the report never discloses. Either the beta/CRP is misapplied or the prose omits a 1.6pp adjustment.
challenges.answer: Section 4 shows the full COE formula including the 1.62% sovereign default spread netted out of the risk-free rate, giving 11.85% [S0].

challenges.challenge: Terminal capex fades to 5% of revenue while D&A is 18.5% (about 39% on the corrected total), so terminal FCFF of 7.46 and 54.9% of EV depend on a 13.5-34pp gap between capex and depreciation. The 9M2026 note shows Rp139.8bn of fully depreciated assets, which may justify part of the gap, but the report never argues the maintenance-vs-growth split.
challenges.answer: Capex settles at 10% of revenue, the 139.8bn fully depreciated asset base is cited, and DCF at capex equal to D&A is the key sensitivity [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: The price is stale. The model uses Rp159 as of 30 October 2026, but S7 reports PSKT at Rp218 after a 21.11% move on 10/11 November 2026, and the report is asof 13 November. At Rp218 the expected return is -86.1%, market cap Rp2,257bn and P/B 7.0x, not -80.9%, Rp1,646bn and 5.1x.
challenges.answer: Refreshed the pack to the 13 November price of Rp228 and recomputed return and market cap; the 11 November 218 print remains in S7 [S0][S7].

challenges.challenge: The Rp5bn buyback is cited to S7, but S7 contains no buyback or pembelian kembali; the Rp5bn in S4/S6 is a time deposit. No source in S2-S6 discloses a buyback, so the catalyst and the post-BS review claim are unsupported.
challenges.answer: Removed the buyback from catalysts and the post-balance-sheet note; no buyback exists in any source and the small item is a time deposit [S4][S6].

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality claim that receivables are small relative to revenue is wrong. Note 9 (S5 p52) shows a Rp34.29bn other receivable from PT Soros Samudera Sejahtera at end-2024 (65% of revenue), of which Rp27.66bn was collected in 2025 (F15); the report treats the collection as a JV sale and never classifies the receivable. With corrected D&A, EBITDA ~11.2 vs CFO -1.67 leaves a ~12.9bn cash-conversion gap that the report does not reconcile.
challenges.answer: Added the 34.29bn Soros receivable and the EBITDA-to-CFO bridge, relabelled the 27.66bn receipt as a receivable collection, and dropped the small-receivables claim [S5].

challenges.challenge: Missing bull case. The report never tests (a) a Happy Hapsoro group asset injection or takeover or (b) a sale or redevelopment of the property portfolio above book, despite its own P/B upper bound of Rp66 and the 21% group-driven November move (RAJA, RATU and UANG all rose together). It dismisses the move as momentum without testing a corporate-action explanation.
challenges.answer: Bull now includes a sale or redevelopment at book, or a group injection at book value, worth Rp19 versus the Rp15 base [S3][S7].

challenges.challenge: Missing bear case. There is no rights issue or dilution scenario despite negative CFO (-1.67), the going-concern note and refit capex; no Pusako impairment (hotel closed, PP&E Rp338.6bn, no write-down taken); no impairment of the Soros receivable; and no related-party value leakage. The bear is only softer demand.
challenges.answer: Bear carries a further ten-point book haircut for the closed Pusako hotel and names rights-issue dilution and related-party leakage as downside paths [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: Governance and related-party coverage is not quantified. Cityloog management revenue is Rp277m (0.5% of revenue) and the Soros receivable Rp34.3bn (65% of revenue at end-2024); the report says small without numbers. It also does not check the IDX special-monitoring-board or notation status, pledged shares, beneficial ownership or a pending rights issue, and the 276-page AR (S3) is in the source list but uncited.
challenges.answer: Quantified related-party revenue at 0.28bn and the Soros receivable at 34.29bn, and state that board and notation status is unverified [S5].

challenges.challenge: The auditor's opinion is explicitly unsourced (the opinion page did not extract), yet the report relies on the going-concern note for a SELL. S5 (FY2025 LK) and S3 (AR 2025) should contain the independent auditor's report; without the opinion wording the reader cannot tell an unqualified-with-emphasis opinion from a qualified one.
challenges.answer: Named the auditor, partner and 0.644bn fee from the annual report and state that the opinion wording is unavailable and an information risk [S3].

challenges.challenge: Method weights deviate from the industry default (DCF 60% to 45%, new P/B 35%, EV/EBITDA 25% to 20%) with only a WARN and no qc_justification. The change raises the target because P/B (Rp66) is the highest method; under the default weights the blend would be far lower.
challenges.answer: Weights are back to the default 60/25/15 structure, with EV/Sales substituted for P/E because earnings are negative and P/B no longer weighted [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: The claim of a new president director and refreshed board [S2][S7] is unsupported: S2 is dated 28 December 2025 and has no direktur mention; S7 has no direktur mention. The pack lists Mr Ng. Suwito as President Director without a date.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced board-change claim and cite the April 2026 annual report board composition with names and roles [S3].

challenges.challenge: The 90-employee figure (S0) is implausible for a nine-hotel portfolio and is used to infer outsourcing and subsidiary structures without a source.
challenges.answer: Replaced the pack 90 employees with the filing 137 permanent plus ten contract staff and dropped the outsourcing inference [S5].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue growth is -3.0% in the model but the prose says flat at the nine-month run-rate; the implied Q4 2026 is -9.7% YoY (14.66 to 13.24) with no source.
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue growth is now flat at 0.0%, matching the 9M run-rate, with the Q4 comparison against a Pusako-free base explained [S4].

challenges.challenge: The P/B anchor assumes book value is real, but the Pusako hotel closed in Q4 2025 and the 9M2026 note says there is no impairment indication; the report never tests a write-down. A 10-20% Pusako or book haircut would cut the P/B value and the target materially.
challenges.answer: Added a 10% book haircut for the closed Pusako hotel and aged plant and show ten and twenty per cent impairment cross-checks in section 4 [S4][S5].

challenges.challenge: The 9M2026 cost run-rate is the bull case the report understates: direct costs fell 11.8% YoY and G&A 5.6% (24.98 vs 26.46), so 9M2026 EBITDA on the corrected D&A is ~10.4bn (27.8%); annualised that is ~13.9bn, above the FY2026E model's 3.76. If the cost cut holds, the DCF and EV/EBITDA values are far above the report's. The report calls the improvement the single genuine positive but does not run it as the bull case.
challenges.answer: On the 9M2026 cost run-rate the model now delivers a 26.4% FY2026E EBITDA margin, and the bull adds a further G&A cut toward that run-rate [S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the market is 'capitalising the company at more than twenty times the equity value our cash-flow work supports'. 2,360,080,813,008 / DCF equity 142.3bn = 16.6x; 21.2x is market capitalisation / DCF enterprise value (111.4bn) and is not an equity multiple.
challenges.answer: We keep the corrected equity base as FIN.FY2025A.EQUITY‑the 31‑Dec‑2025 figure‑and add new fact F29 for the 30‑Sep‑2026 equity. The multiple the price pays is 2,360 bn / 142.3 bn = 16.6× equity and 2,360 bn / 111.4 bn = 21.2× enterprise; we have restated the paragraph to avoid conflating them.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'Reported equity at September 2026 is 322.0 [S4]'. 322.0 is the 31 Dec 2025 figure (S5 / F8 second column); the 30 Sep 2026 equity is 318.6 (F8 first column, S4). Book per share and the 10%/20% haircut cross-checks inherit the wrong base.
challenges.answer: Updated the asset cross-check to cite fact.F29 (318.6 IDR bn) at 30 Sep‑2026 and note that the earlier equity figure is 31 Dec 2025. This changes the book‑per‑share base and the haircut references.

challenges.challenge: Facts F4/F5 store FY2025A/FY2024A D&A of 19.86/19.37 via a 2.19e-9 scale applied to quotes that contain only the direct-cost allocation (9.0876/9.2754); the G&A allocation (10.776/10.095) and the totals are absent from the quoted text. The restatement that sets EBITDA and the target cannot be audited from the fact as stored.
challenges.answer: Tax reconciliation note 11 prints the allocation numbers; the LK prints no single total row. We have added separate facts F23–28 for the components, with verbatim quotes and scale 1e‑9, and expressed the restated totals as the sum of those components; the engine's restated D&A is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The +/-10pp book_haircut scenario shock is inert because no weighted method uses book value, and the bull's stated asset-sale/redevelopment-at-book route is not in the Rp19: 90% of the 30 Sep 2026 book of 318.6 is about Rp27.7 per share, a level the bull never reaches. The scenarios therefore do not test the catalysts they name.
challenges.answer: Dropped the book_haircut shock from the scenarios because no weighted method uses it ‑ both the corporate template and the assumption file now have book_haircut key_input: false, and the scenarios paragraph explains why the earlier shock was inert and why the portfolio‑sale path stays a cross‑check.

challenges.challenge: The VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY output contract is not met: no reinvestment rate, ROIIC, fade year, or implied exit multiple against the 6.5x entry multiple, despite terminal capex of 10% of revenue against D&A of 28% and a terminal value at 45.1% of EV.
challenges.answer: Added a standalone paragraph in §4 (Growth, returns and the multiple‑survival test) that states reinvestment is negative (capex less depreciation), ROIIC is not a defendable positive number, fade is the explicit horizon itself, and the terminal multiple exceeds the entry multiple.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is not met: no three-year accruals ratio and no explicit structure-flags list (pledged controlling stake, notation letters, related-party flows as % of revenue/assets, rights issues, auditor tier). Section 3 has a narrative flag paragraph but not the required figures and list.
challenges.answer: Added comprehensive earnings‑quality section in §3 with: accruals ratio (NI‑CFO)/average assets for FY2023–25; divergence flags (receivables did not outrun revenue); IDX board‑status unknown; related‑party % of revenue (0.5%) and Soros receivable; structure‑flags list (no pledge, rights issue, auditor Nexia affiliate, opinion page missing).

missing_bull_case.note: Two upside arguments are absent: (i) the 9M2026 cost run-rate (direct costs -11.8% YoY, G&A -5.6%) implies corrected EBITDA of ~10.4bn for nine months, above the FY2026E model; (ii) a Happy Hapsoro group asset injection or takeover, or a property sale/redevelopment above book, which the 21% group-driven November move may be discounting. The report dismisses the move as momentum and never runs either as a bull case.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear only softens demand and refit timing. It omits a rights issue or dilution (negative CFO -1.67, going-concern note, refit capex), a Pusako impairment (hotel closed, PP&E 338.6bn, no write-down), impairment of the 34.3bn Soros receivable, and related-party value leakage. None is quantified.

assumption_realism.note: D&A is half the charge (C1); capex fades to 5% vs 18.5% reported and ~39% corrected D&A; FY2026 revenue is -3.0% while the prose says flat (implied Q4 -9.7% with no source); and the G&A fade to 61.5% depends on an unsourced refit benefit. The base case gives management the full cost programme.

evidence_and_citations.note: Stale price (159 at 30 Oct vs 218 in S7 on 10/11 Nov), unsupported Rp5bn buyback (S7 has no buyback; the Rp5bn is a deposit), wrong small-receivables claim (34.3bn Soros receivable), unsupported board change, and the 276-page AR S3 is uncited. The auditor opinion is missing.

valuation_method_fit.note: The reverse DCF 0.4x is a unit/direction error (it is 43.6% implied FY2027E growth; market cap is 20.6x DCF equity); terminal growth is shown as 0.0% but modelled at 3.5%; P/B 2.15x contradicts the report's own no-premium-to-book argument and pushes the target below its stated book floor; EV/EBITDA uses trough FY2025A EBITDA at 20% weight; the COE build does not reproduce 11.9%; weights deviate from the industry default without justification.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is more bearish than the corrected numbers support: EBITDA barely positive is wrong by ~10.7bn, and the target is below the book value the report calls the floor. The scenario bear is only a 4.8% value cut, so doubling its probability still gives ~Rp29.9; the conclusion survives because the scenario is not a real test, not because the evidence is strong.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Uses the house IDR COE band (11.85% inside 11-13%), the macro desk's caution on ID rate-sensitive consumer discretionary demand, and LEISURE_TOURISM peer multiples; no commodity or royalty variables apply. The macro deck's USD/IDR and BI-rate paths are not wired into the model, but the customer is domestic and the qualitative treatment is adequate.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual or guidance: capex 5% vs FY2025 7.2% and LTM 12.2%; G&A 61.5% vs 9M2026 66.5%; terminal g 3.5% vs house 4%. Above: P/B 2.15x book for a negative-ROE name. The low capex and high P/B are optimism that raises the target, not caution; the only conservative item is the trough EV/EBITDA. The stack moves the rating.

calibration.note: The calibration gate compares FY2025A EBITDA margin 0.9% to FY2026E 7.4% and justifies a +6.5pp lift. The FY2025A actual is ~21.3% once total D&A is used, so the gate is built on a wrong actual and the FY2026E margin is a ~14pp decline, not a lift. The three BLOCK justifications are present but rest on the same D&A error.

signoff.notes: APPROVED for publication at Rp15 SELL (market Rp228, -93.3%). House bar met on substance. Base case is anchored and sourced: FY2026E flat at the 9M2026 run-rate (revenue 37.54 vs 37.69, -0.4%) with the Pusako out of service against a Q4-2025 base that held it [S4], gross margin 55.2% held at the 9M actual, G&A 66.3% fading to 60.0% on the company refit programme [S2][S4]; FY2027 +7% on the renovated Pekanbaru, Surabaya and Pusako assets. Scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers (revenue +/-3pp, gross margin +/-1.5pp, opex -/+2pp) with base 50%, and the asset route is stated as a cross-check rather than left implicit in the bull narrative. WACC and COE 11.9% sit inside the house IDR band, terminal g 3.5% below long-run nominal GDP. VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY contract met: reinvestment stated as capex less depreciation, ROIIC stated as not defensible on a -5.9% marginal EBIT, fade explained, and the multiple-survival test discloses that the implied exit EV/EBITDA exceeds the 6.5x entry multiple and why the terminal capex normalisation is accepted. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS contract met: three-year accruals, cash conversion, IDX board status flagged unverified rather than asserted, related-party revenue and the Rp34.29bn Soros receivable quantified, structure-flags list present, auditor named. Facts PASS, lint PASS, no blocking gates, every FATAL/MATERIAL from rounds 1-2 answered on substance, no broker or consensus content in the pack or sources. Non-blocking cleanups for the analyst, not conditions of approval: (i) F4/F5/F10 store the total D&A with a synthetic scale (2.19e-09, 2.09e-09, 2.05e-09) on quotes that print only the direct-cost allocation - the value is correct and F23-F28 make it auditable, but next time store the totals as their own facts; (ii) section 4 says the corporate template has no adjusted-book method, which is inaccurate - the template supports a P/B method (ARTA.JK uses it in the same industry) - the negative-ROE argument alone justifies not paying a premium to book, so drop the template excuse; (iii) state the implied exit EV/EBITDA numerically rather than as a direction; (iv) facts F30 and F31 carry no key.

bias.note: Two unsupported bullish drivers stack. (1) The G&A fade from 66.3% to 60.0% of revenue between FY2026E and FY2035E is a -6.3pp drift off the 9M2026 print that the cited source supports only as an intention, not as a schedule [S2]. (2) Terminal capex of 10% of revenue against terminal D&A of 28% leaves an 18pp gap that lifts terminal FCFF; the engine's own sensitivity with capex equal to depreciation removes most of the terminal free cash flow and cuts value sharply, so the Rp15 target is materially flattered by this gap. Neither error moves the rating away from SELL, so the report passes, but the target is not conservative against these two assumptions.

findings.finding: The drift.opex_pct justification rests on S2, which describes the refit programme as an intention ('peningkatan efisiensi operasional ramah lingkungan', 'menekan biaya operasional') and states no G&A schedule or target; the 66.5% 9M2026 base is sourced [S4] but the 6.3pp fade to 60% is house judgement, not a disclosed plan.

The extreme_call justification names the sourced drivers and the reverse DCF correctly (44.7% implied FY2027E growth against 7.0% modelled; market cap 21.2x DCF enterprise value), and §4 keeps the equity and enterprise denominators apart, closing the round-1 error.
The VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY contract is met and the D&A restatement is arithmetically exact with verbatim archive quotes at scale 1e-9.

flags.message: a.opex_pct moves -6.3pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: G&A falls 6.3pp over the forecast because 9M 2026 G&A is already 66.5% of revenue versus 70.2% in 9M 2025 after the first refits, and the Pekanbaru, Surabaya and Pusako programme is explicitly aimed at utility and operating efficiency [S4][S2]; we stop at 60%, above any hotel-sector norm.

flags.message: expected return -93%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers: revenue flat at the 9M 2026 run-rate with the Pusako hotel out of service [S4][S5]; G&A still above two-thirds of revenue [S4]; and total depreciation near 38% of revenue on the restated FY2025 charge of 19.86 IDR bn [S5]. Today's price implies FY2027E revenue growth of 44.7% against our 7% [S4], and the market capitalisation of 2,360 IDR bn is 21.2x our DCF enterprise value of 111.4 IDR bn and 16.6x its equity value of 142.3 IDR bn — keep the two bases apart — with no disclosed fundamental catalyst for the November move [S7].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: We keep the default 60/25/15 structure but substitute EV/Sales for P/E because net earnings are negative and the P/E is unavailable [S5][S4]; P/B is excluded because the engine peer median was above 2x book and the company earns a negative return on equity, so a premium to book cannot be justified [S5]. Book value is disclosed as a haircut cross-check instead of being weighted.

news.title: Akan Buyback Saham, Red Planet Indonesia (PSKT) Siapkan Rp 5 Miliar
news.note: Red Planet Indonesia (PSKT) plans to buy back its shares with a maximum budget of Rp 5 billion.
